items.claim: C1.2-C1.4 measured the fixed prefix on deepseek-flash before any settings change and after both levers: before_prefix 43982 (two runs, stable), after_deny_prefix 43189 (kept the second of two runs after writing permissions.deny only; the first of that pair read 32176, a low outlier discarded per the run-twice-keep-second protocol), after_prefix 43189 (two runs after enabledPlugins was also written, both stable at the same value as the kept after-deny run). delta = before_prefix - after_prefix = 793 tokens (1.8%), positive as required. The Verification-step live re-check (live_c1_measure.py, a fresh run) read 43259, also below before_prefix. Scale matches the brief's P2 reference (707 tokens, 1.76%) rather than the 70K figure the Ruling's prose might suggest.

C1.3 set enabledPlugins['voltagent-meta@voltagent-subagents'] to false because c1-counts.tsv's SUBAGENT TYPES section has zero voltagent-meta: rows. superpowers@superpowers-marketplace got no entry (so it keeps inheriting the operator's user-level true) because the same file shows 8 superpowers: skill calls across 4 distinct skills plus 1 superpowers:code-reviewer subagent call, so the brief's zero-both condition for disabling it is false.

C1.3 added 10 permissions.deny entries, one mcp__<server> per zero-30-day-call candidate: github, claude-context, context7, sequential-thinking, supabase, mcp-registry, scheduled-tasks, and three connector ids (1a59c906.., d225a347.., 6f616b42..). The other 3 candidates stayed allowed because c1-counts.tsv shows nonzero 30-day calls: desktop-commander 1, chrome-devtools 346, the Vercel connector 326cc715.. 43. No keep-list server (ccd_*, Claude_Browser, visualize, terminal, claude-in-chrome, computer-use, plugin_premium-web_*) was touched; test_c1_settings.py case 4 checks this directly.

test_c1_settings.py implements the brief's four C1.5 checks and passes 4/4; it additionally hardcodes the live hook wiring's shape (4 event keys, 11 hook groups, 10 distinct script basenames) as its reading of the brief's 'still has ... its hook entries,' since the brief did not give an exact shape to check against.
live_c1_measure.py runs measure-prefix.ps1 once more with a fresh temp HARNESS_STATE_DIR and passes when the fresh prefix reads below c1-measure.json's before_prefix; it does (43259 < 43982).

Pre-flight held on entry to part 2: python 3.14.0, node v22.20.0, claude at the recorded path, PowerShell 5.1.22621.6133, LOCALAPPDATA unchanged, no node_modules; usage_audit.py present; settings.json read 22 False False, confirming C1.3 had not yet run. scripts/harness/tests/test_*.py counted 16, not the 13 the brief's own snapshot recorded 2026-09-22 20:05 UTC -- runs G, H and a cross-review fix commit landed on top of that snapshot (plus run F part 1's own +1) before this dispatch started; the two actual bulleted pre-flight commands, the only ones stated as live gates, both matched, so this was not treated as a return condition. Also ran python .claude/hooks/routing-reminder.py directly (outside the formal Verification list) against the Return Conditions' premium-web-gate clause after denying servers and disabling voltagent-meta; it still printed the routing table.

run_all.py passes all 17 offline test files (the 16 present at part-2 start plus test_c1_settings.py); diff_scope.py confirms the 4 paths this part touched before the digest rewrite (.claude/settings.json, .planning/harness/c1-measure.json, scripts/harness/tests/test_c1_settings.py, scripts/harness/tests/live_c1_measure.py) are all on the brief's Files list.

tests.last_line: PASS diff scope: 4 changed paths, all listed

deviations: c1-measure.json's denied_servers lists bare server names (e.g. 'github'), not the 'mcp__<server>' deny-entry strings; the brief's JSON template left the shape open, and this reads more naturally next to disabled_plugins' plugin ids.

enabledPlugins carries only the one entry the brief's stated condition actually set false (voltagent-meta@voltagent-subagents); superpowers@superpowers-marketplace, whose zero-both condition was false, was left out entirely rather than added as an explicit true, matching C1.3's 'change nothing else' line with the smaller diff.

test_c1_settings.py case 1 hardcodes the hook wiring's exact current shape (event keys, group count, script basenames) as its reading of 'still has ... its hook entries'; this makes the check strict against a future hook rename as well as against this run's own edits.

Ran python .claude/hooks/routing-reminder.py once, outside the formal Verification list, as a direct probe of the Return Conditions' premium-web-gate clause; it still printed the routing table (see items).
